score: equivalent: 51 of 65 proved clean, 8 proved under a disclosed assumption, 5 unproved (one the emulator refutes through its CAST bug, which the guard demotes), 0 refuted; not equivalent: 11 of 26 refuted, 1 demoted by the guard, 10 missed, 3 proved only under the disclosed no-NaN assumption, 1 emulator error; 21 error-class cases unscored
baseline: before the proof layers (refutation only, with literal harvesting): 0 proved, 12 of 26 refuted, 13 missed, 1 wrong (2026-11-12 morning)
with_specials: with --specials (tuned on test): 13 of 26 refuted, 12 missed, 2 wrong. The extra wrong is a label question: SUM over FLOAT64 depends on addition order, and the pair float-sum-union-branches-swapped is labelled equivalent
caveats: Before the guard the 1 wrong was the emulator, not the prover: CAST(FLOAT64 AS INT64) truncates where real BigQuery rounds half away from zero (2.5 gives 2, BigQuery 3). Proofs come from the layers ported from Kumo_SQL_Prover (docs/ported-layers.md); proved means no layer's assumption list names an assumption the case violates. 11 pairs are proved only under a disclosed assumption and count as unknown: 3 NaN pairs (the prover assumes FLOAT64 is never NaN, and the emulator cannot hold NaN so it cannot check) and 8 float-sum pairs (the prover treats SUM as independent of row order, which BigQuery does not promise: the open FLOAT64 SUM labelling question for Walter). The first run of the ported layers proved float-sum-pre-aggregated, a false proof (the algebraic layer regroups FLOAT64 partial sums as if addition were associative); the emulator did not catch it on random data, only the label did. The layer is now skipped for any pair that may sum a FLOAT64. 2 proofs are withheld because the algebraic layer cannot compare runtime errors (int-sum-pre-aggregated, float-avg-versus-sum-over-count). Refutation: 8 seeded random databases plus the case's witness rows. Two label problems found against real BigQuery: ten-decimal NUMERIC literals are rejected (numeric-literal-rounding, numeric-literal-below-half). Development set, no held-out split; the earlier prover's rules were tuned on these cases (tuned on test).
guard: With the trust guard: cast-versus-round (CAST(FLOAT64 AS INT64) truncates on the emulator) is demoted instead of refuted, so wrong is 0; safe-divide-versus-filter is demoted. Before the guard: 12 of 26 refuted, 1 wrong. Proofs are unchanged (51 proved, 0 false proofs). The base FLOAT64 pool no longer holds 1e308 (odd-seeded databases add it).
